born.why: The code prioritizes survival by checking starvation levels first, then uses diary data to distinguish safe from poisonous species based on harm counts and benefit magnitudes, switching to cautious tasting for unknowns when hunger allows, and exploiting known safe fruits via eating or carrying.

The code improves safety by rejecting high-risk foods even when hungry (unless starving) and uses Bayesian smoothing for better risk estimation, ensuring Fagi prioritizes long-term survival over short-term gains on uncertain fruits.

This code prioritizes learning by tasting uncertain fruits only when safe from starvation, leverages positive history to stockpile known-safe food via 'carry', and strictly avoids known poisons, optimizing long-term survival and efficiency.

The code prioritizes survival by eating only when critically hungry, uses tasting for safe data gathering on unknown fruits when feasible, and leverages the pantry mechanism to store known-safe food for future hunger spikes, while strictly avoiding identified poisonous species.

The code prioritizes survival by using a safer threshold for tasting (hunger > 30) and requires more evidence (3 safe samples) before trusting a fruit species enough to carry it, while still allowing risky eating when starvation is imminent.

The code prioritizes survival by avoiding known poisons and starving to death, while using tasting to safely identify new food sources when hunger allows, and caching safe foods when immediate hunger is low to preserve stomach capacity for future exploration.
